Printed corrugated boxes

Planning a full color corrugated mailer and product kit

FORME Packaging editorialUpdated October 21, 20263 min read

A die-cut mailer combines presentation with a repeatable packing action. Plan the lid, folded sidewalls, locking flap, insert and artwork together.

In this guideConfirm the die-cut constructionArrange the kit before sizing the mailerUse the inside as a deliberate printed surfaceTest packing and shipmentDiscuss your packaging →

Confirm the die-cut construction

A common roll-end mailer uses a rear-hinged lid, folded sidewalls and a front closure. The side flaps and locking details depend on the chosen drawing. Review the assembled structure, rather than assuming every box described as a “mailer” has identical tabs and folds.

Fine-flute corrugated board is visibly different from thin solid white card and from wrapped rigid board. Ask for the proposed flute and liner combination. Check exposed cut edges and folded corners on a physical sample.

Arrange the kit before sizing the mailer

List all contents, including cards, tissue and small accessories. Place heavier pieces where the insert can support them and provide a separate space for items that could scratch one another. Confirm enough access to remove the first product without pulling out the entire tray.

Subscription packs need a repeatable arrangement. If the contents change, identify the size range the insert must accommodate and decide whether alternative inserts are needed. Test both the smallest and largest planned assortment.

Use the inside as a deliberate printed surface

Exterior artwork introduces the brand, while the open lid can carry a concise message or pattern. Check its orientation on an erected sample. Artwork that reads correctly on the flat die line may appear upside down when the lid opens.

Allow for folds, locking tabs and areas covered by the sidewalls. Large solids need review around rubbing points and fold edges. Confirm whether both sides of the board are printed and how the color reference will be approved.

Test packing and shipment

  • Assemble several samples using the intended packing method.
  • Check that tabs locate without tearing or excessive force.
  • Load all contents and inspect product movement.
  • Confirm the closure and any extra sealing or outer packaging.
  • Review the packed dimensions and delivery requirements.

See the corrugated box series for beauty kits, apparel, electronics, tea and corporate welcome packs.
